etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French coïncider, from Medieval Latin coincidere, from con- + incidere, from in- (“into, to”) + cadere (“to fall, fall down, drop”).

definitions.definition: To occupy exactly the same space.
To occur at the same time.

quote.citation: 1952 December, R. C. Riley, “By Rail to Kemp Town”, in Railway Magazine, page 835:
quote.text: The last train ran on December 31, 1932, almost unnoticed, for it coincided with the running of the last steam passenger train down the main line from London to Brighton, a much more momentous event.
